newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end mixed, eye on upcoming data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end mixed, eye on upcoming data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed mixed in quiet trade on Monday, with the yield curve steepening slightly and investors largely focused on economic data being released later this week, dealers said.

"Our currency is in pretty good shape still and so I think that's a little bit supportive," said Rich Wylie, a fixed-income economist with TD Securities Inc. "Most investors are inclined to say let's see what we get out of the numbers because we do have a fairly large schedule of releases."
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$0.10 to C$107.50 to yield 7.351 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 4/32 to yield 6.86 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to 49 basis points from 50 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.

Both Canadian and U.S. bonds opened stronger this morning, aided by an appreciation in North American currencies in overnight trade. However, Canadian bonds later weakened as U.S. Treasury prices moved lower.

Canadian bond investors are now focusing on key U.S. inflation and retail sales data being released on Tuesday. Investors are especially sensitive to new data after Friday's stronger-than-expected U.S. employment report, analysts said.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.03 to C$102.05 to yield 6.711 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.62 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to nine basis points from 10 basis points at Friday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded with a yield of 2.87 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.17 percent.
